title: This Robot Hand Feels a Grip Slipping
description: Eka Robotics announced a 150 million dollar Series A for a vision-force-action model that adds touch feedback to robot grasping. It is trained mostly by reinforcement learning in simulation. Performance figures are company claims.

beats.text: A robot hand that feels slipping
beats.vo: This robot hand can feel an object starting to slip, and tighten its grip before it falls.

beats.text: Company claim, on objects it never trained on
beats.vo: Eka Robotics says its system makes about fifteen hundred picks an hour on unseen objects. A human manages about six hundred. These are company claims, not independently verified.
Follow for a daily dose of engineering.

caption:
A robot hand that can feel a grip slipping 🤖
Eka Robotics raised $150M for a model that mixes vision with touch, trained mostly in simulation. Claimed: ~1,500 picks/hour on unseen objects. Company numbers, not independently verified; long-term factory reliability is still unproven.
